absent: Microcode firmware request, collection, apply, staging and finalization internals beyond callback signatures.
Numeric values of Hyper-V SynIC and nested MSRs and SynIC field layouts.
Hypercall page setup, VP assist handling, and isolated VM read write helpers.
Native helpers for SMP stop, APIC EOI, interrupt stats, UV init, IOMMU shutdown and encrypted guest hooks.
HPET base mapping, channel count, and boot config initialization.
CPU topology matching predicates and mask allocation failure handling.
Locking and concurrency for handler install and remove and for sibling mask updates.

findings.text: Microcode operations table carries callbacks for firmware request and per CPU teardown plus apply and staging and info collection and late load finalization, with three one bit options for NMI safety and NMI use and staging use. Core layer promises the latter group always executes on the target CPU.

Update outcome vocabulary starts at zero for success and then distinguishes freshly found images and safe fresh images from already updated state and from missing images and from hard error and timeout and offline target. Callers use these values to decide retry and promotion.
Early load record keeps a pair of revision numbers describing the version observed before loading and the version selected after loading.
Maximum number of microcode blobs handled in one scan is one hundred twenty eight.

Four byte packing places first byte lowest and fourth byte highest with eight bit shifts. Intel vendor identity is split over three such words spelling the expected twelve letter name and AMD vendor identity is split likewise over three words spelling its twelve letter name.
Intel operations instance connects request and collection and late apply and late finalization and staging handlers and enables the NMI based path only for sixty four bit builds.
Internal header uses a single include guard macro and provides an empty inline teardown for AMD when that support is not built in, so callers can invoke it unconditionally.

Public SynIC register interface offers read and write helpers for nested and non nested cases plus paravisor direct accessors and a toggle for SINT proxy mode. Reads return a sixty four bit value and writes accept register number with value.

When nested virtualization is active a translation step rewrites SynIC interrupt configuration registers by offset and rewrites five control registers for message page and event page and version and control and end of message to their nested counterparts, leaving all other numbers unchanged.

For SynIC registers with a paravisor present, reads use the isolated VM read helper and writes use the isolated VM write helper, with an extra native write for interrupt configuration registers to propagate the proxy flag from the cached boolean.

Direct paravisor register helpers require both paravisor presence and a SynIC register number, otherwise they warn. The read path then returns all bits set and the write path returns without action, while valid calls use native register access.

Two system vectors provide Hyper-V entry. The callback vector saves interrupt registers and accounts a callback statistic and invokes management and VMBus handlers when installed and mixes interrupt randomness and conditionally signals end of interrupt when the deprecating auto end hint is set. The timer zero vector similarly accounts and invokes its handler and always signals end of interrupt. Both restore prior registers.

Modules can install callbacks for management and VMBus and timer zero and kexec and crash, with matching removal for all but management. VMBus and timer removal only clears the stored pointer because the interrupt gate cannot be freed.

Hyper-V shutdown on kexec first cleans timer state globally and runs the kexec callback, then removes the Hyper-V online CPU hotplug state to avoid later corruption of assist pages, then delegates to native shutdown which stops other CPUs, and finally tears down the hypercall page once a single CPU remains.

Native shutdown begins encrypted guest preparation while all CPUs run, then quiets the IO APIC before the local APIC, then on multiprocessor disables local interrupts and stops peers, then shuts the local APIC and restores boot interrupt mode and disables the high precision timer and on sixty four bit shuts the IOMMU, finishing with encrypted guest completion when kexec is in progress.

High precision timer disable is a no-op when boot disabled or address missing or unmapped, otherwise it clears the global enable while preserving boot config, restores each channel boot config, and reasserts the boot config when the timer was enabled at boot. Register writes go through a small helper adding offset to the mapped base.

Guest crash path under Hyper-V runs the registered crash callback with trap registers, then native crash shutdown, then hypercall cleanup. Native crash shutdown assumes a broken kernel, disables interrupts, stops secondaries once, disables confidential and virtualization and tracing facilities, clears IO APIC locks and interrupts, shuts local APIC, restores boot mode, disables timer, runs encrypted guest begin and finish back to back, and saves crashing CPU state.
Symmetric crash stop is idempotent through a static done flag and prefers a platform crash stop hook when present, falling back to generic stop. The uniprocessor build provides an empty variant.

Suspend captures the Hyper-V reference counter and resume adjusts the scheduler clock offset by the suspend value minus the current value to account for hibernation time. Wrapper save and restore chain the prior platform hooks around these steps and installation occurs only when the reference TSC feature is advertised, preserving old hooks for chaining.
Hypercall updater has two build flavors, one refreshing a static call target for the hypercall and one discarding its argument as a null statement.

Platform probe requires the hypervisor CPU flag, then checks the vendor leaf range and twelve byte vendor signature, then requires hypercall and virtual processor index features with warnings on absence, returning the vendor leaf identifier on success and zero otherwise.

Unknown NMI filter returns done immediately when panic on unknown is disabled, otherwise exactly one CPU wins a compare exchange from negative one to its own id and returns done to allow panic while all losers report handled.
Time stamp frequency helper reads the Hyper-V frequency register and scales hertz down to kilohertz by division.

Hyper-V boot CPU preparation delegates to native preparation and then initializes paravirtual spinlocks on sixty four bit builds with that option. Native preparation handles per CPU base switching on uniprocessor and always initializes paravirtual lock state, which enables the virtual spinlock branch when running as a guest.

Hyper-V secondary preparation starts with native preparation, then for SNP isolation without paravisor overrides the sixty four bit secondary wakeup hook and returns, then detects kexec reuse by single present CPU or existing logical processor and returns, otherwise adds each non boot logical processor and notifies all started and creates each virtual processor, treating failures as fatal.

Native secondary preparation runs common allocation, then branches on interrupt mode to disable SMP for legacy or unrouted modes with timer setup in one subcase, otherwise sets up per CPU clocks and announces boot CPU details and initializes UV platform and calibrates init delay and initializes store bypass sharing and installs the SNP wakeup hook.

Store bypass initialization clears local state, preserves already established sharing across hotplug, initializes the per CPU lock once, then links to an existing sibling shared record when a sibling on the same core already created one, otherwise self links as the first sibling so later siblings can join.

Init delay calibration honors a command line override, selects zero delay for recent Intel and Hygon and AMD families by vendor and model thresholds, and falls back to a legacy ten millisecond delay for older parts.

SMP disable path logs the event, disables IO APIC support, narrows present and possible sets to the boot CPU, clears the physical APIC presence bitmap and re marks the boot APIC when valid, and marks sibling and core and die sharing masks for CPU zero.

Common SMP preparation marks every non boot possible CPU as hotpluggable by an out of range index, allocates sibling and core and die and last level and second level sharing masks on the owning node, and establishes the initial sibling map for CPU zero.

Sibling map builder records the CPU in the setup mask, uses a fast path for single thread single core parts to self link all sharing masks and set booted core count to one, otherwise links sibling and cache and die masks against prior CPUs with a package node sanity check, refreshes maximum thread counts and active flags, then in a second pass links package core masks and maintains booted core counts for new cores versus new threads.
Node equality test resolves each CPU descriptor index to its NUMA node and reports whether both nodes match.

Fragile orderings include quieting IO APIC before local APIC to avoid an Atom erratum hang, stopping peers before LAPIC and timer teardown, requiring hypercall and VP index features before Hyper-V use, fatal handling of logical and virtual processor creation errors, warn and fail on invalid paravisor register use, and inability to free VMBus and timer gates so removal only nulls the callback.
